findings.claim: The placement change updated module.json and the README but left seven lab placement statements in this module's topic catalog saying the lab is on S12, which now contradicts the module's own placement note (lab after S13 row 0, before S13 row 1) and README line 5. The review topic.json lab reason (line 66) says Task 7 is in "the api-security module lab (S12)". The artifacts.lab.reason of each of the six S12 topics (session-cookies-vs-jwts-trade-offs line 66, password-hashing line 66, issuing-and-checking-a-jwt line 67, role-protected-endpoints line 67, a-dev-profile-that-keeps-endpoints-open-during-front-end-work line 67, common-api-security-risks-owasp line 66) says "practised in the planned api-security module lab (Standard lab overlay, S12), authored in the api-security module PR", which is also stale because the lab is authored. How it is reached: not by a learner on the documented path, since no learner page names the lab or its day (critic grep of every artifact.md/html/gift in the module). It is reached by the taxonomy/workbook owner, to whom module.json routes the replacement placement, or by anyone reading the topic catalog, who finds two placements for one lab. Low: metadata only, and the README a learner reads is correct.
findings.recommendation: In the same module branch, reword each lab absence reason to the end-of-module placement (for example: practised in the api-security module coding lab, Standard, placed after the S13 review page), drop "planned" and "authored in the api-security module PR", then relock the module.

findings.claim: The new S13 budget note sums authored minutes against the 120-minute day (review page 14, lab 60, module check 45 = 119), which is the repository convention (intake Minute budgets: budgets mapped to a day must fit the day type's 120-minute block total; S13 was 14 + 45 = 59 before this change). What it does not record is where the 60-minute lab sits in the S13 day template. S13 is dayType "Review" (snapshot tracks[1].weeks[2].days[2]), whose blocks are Cumulative quiz 15, Error-log review 20, Practice without AI 25, Module check 45, and Reflection and next-week plan 15. The template has no coding-lab block longer than 25 minutes, and 1 minute is left for the four non-check blocks. The previous placement had a home in the S12 Lab template's 85-minute Guided lab block, and the intake maps every other lab or project into a named block (S6 Build 80, FT5/FT7 Guided 85). Meanwhile the review topic.json still justifies two absences with S13 template blocks: gift (line 58: "the S13 Review day has its own cumulative quiz block") and lab (line 66: "the S13 Review day's Practice without AI platform block"). If the lab displaces those blocks, both reasons now cite blocks whose fate nothing records. How a learner reaches it: only through the workbook owner's build of S13. README line 9 ("so the Spring module check still starts on time") is true under the captain's three-item day, but if the platform keeps the Review template's blocks before the module check and adds the lab, a learner who follows the 60-minute rule still reaches the check late. Low: the risk is a record gap in the placement handed to the workbook owner, not a defect in the lab.

evidence.section: Minute budgets (day budgets fit the day type block total) and lab block mappings

findings.recommendation: Do not change the lab. In module.json's S13 note, record which Review template blocks the 60-minute lab replaces on Standard S13 (cumulative quiz, error-log review, practice without AI, reflection, or the template as a whole), confirmed by the captain, so the workbook owner builds the day that README line 9 assumes. Then reword the review topic.json gift and lab absence reasons so they do not cite blocks the new S13 no longer holds, and relock.
